answer: The trusted grader set grows only through bootstrap capacity, so new aliases cannot immediately capture majority control — there is a warm-up period where established agents hold the jury, preventing a sudden Sybil takeover. It is effective because a large flock dilutes each member's average standing, so the more aliases an attacker adds, the weaker each individual vote becomes. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable. Consider a river as the anchor of the cost.
